response.sql: WITH rental_payments AS (SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) as rental_payment_total FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id LEFT JOIN payment p ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id), store_averages AS (SELECT store_id, AVG(rental_payment_total) as store_avg FROM rental_payments GROUP BY store_id) SELECT rp.store_id, SUM(rp.rental_payment_total) as sum_of_totals, AVG(rp.rental_payment_total - sa.store_avg) as avg_excess FROM rental_payments rp JOIN store_averages sa ON rp.store_id = sa.store_id WHERE rp.rental_payment_total > sa.store_avg GROUP BY rp.store_id

assumptions.assumption: Rentals without any linked payments are represented as NULL payment totals. AVG() ignores these NULLs when computing the store-specific average, and the WHERE clause excludes them (NULL > average is never true). This interpretation aligns with "Averages ignore missing values."

alternatives.interpretation: Rentals without linked payments should be treated as having payment total 0 (not NULL), so they are included in the store-specific average calculation. This would lower the average when a store has rentals with no payments.
alternatives.sql: WITH rental_payments AS (SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, COALESCE(SUM(p.amount), 0) as rental_payment_total FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id LEFT JOIN payment p ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id), store_averages AS (SELECT store_id, AVG(rental_payment_total) as store_avg FROM rental_payments GROUP BY store_id) SELECT rp.store_id, SUM(rp.rental_payment_total) as sum_of_totals, AVG(rp.rental_payment_total - sa.store_avg) as avg_excess FROM rental_payments rp JOIN store_averages sa ON rp.store_id = sa.store_id WHERE rp.rental_payment_total > sa.store_avg GROUP BY rp.store_id
